chunks: And in it, that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except over those who follow him.
And He made for them partners in their souls to mislead them from what He gave them.
And His authority over them is only so that We may know who believes in the Hereafter from he who is in doubt about it.
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of Satan's authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this hadith within the Shia doctrine of *Khufra* (subtle authority), clarifying that Satan's influence is not coercive but persuasive, targeting the will of those who voluntarily align with his whispers. This distinction underscores the theological principle that faith is a choice, serving as a divine trial to separate the steadfast believers from those whose hearts are susceptible to doubt and spiritual negligence.
